To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) EMG indices of back muscle weakness and fiber composition are not affected by low back pain status; 2) EMG indices that are sensitive to fatigue may be useful to detect gender-related differences in fatigability; 3) the prediction of back muscle strength from EMG fatigue indices is not reliable; and 4) a better prediction of back muscle maximal strength may be obtained from anthropometric measures.
(1) the EMG indices used in this study are reliable and (2) they are insensitive to low back pain and gender.

(1) surface EMG can be used to assess weakness, muscle fiber type composition and fatigibility in the lumbar and abdominal muscles and (2) these assessments are reliable, but insensitive to low back pain or gender.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reliable and valid surface electromyography assessment protocol for back muscles.

the reliability of the EMG parameters used in this study, the sensitivity of the different indices to the status of low back pain and gender, the use of anthropometry to predict back strength, the effect of low back pain on back muscle strength and the effect of gender on muscle fatigability.
the development of EMG indices that are reliable and sensitive to the assessment of weakness, fiber composition, and fatigability in back muscles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reliability of EMG indices for the assessment of weakness, fiber composition, and fatigability of back muscles is acceptable.
the EMG assessment of back muscle properties is feasible but that further research is required to optimize the measurement strategy.
EMG assessment of intrinsic muscle properties is a promising tool for back muscle assessment, but that it is not yet fully developed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EMG assessment of back muscle strength, fiber composition and fatiguability can be reliable and sensitive to the effects of gender but not to the effects of low back status.
EMG indices can provide reliable measures of muscle weakness, fiber composition, and fatigability, but that these measures are not sensitive to gender or back pain status.

, with proper attention to the measurement strategy, the surface EMG technique is a reliable tool that could be used to assess weakness, muscle fiber type composition and fatigabilty in the back extensor muscles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
surface EMG is a valid and reliable tool to assess back muscle weakness, fiber composition, fatigability and maximal strength.
the assessment of intrinsic back muscle properties using surface EMG is a challenging endeavor.

EMG assessment of back muscle strength and fatigue is feasible but that the use of absolute loads is problematic and that the prediction of maximal back strength from EMG fatigue indices is still in need of further development.
